# # Support Ticket: Services failing to connect to backend

**Priority:** High
**Submitted by:** DevOps Team Lead
**Product:** Internal API Gateway (Envoy-based)

---

Hi support,

We've been seeing intermittent failures hitting our backend services through the proxy layer. During peak traffic windows (usually around 2-4pm), a bunch of requests start failing and our monitoring shows the error "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: overflow."

It seems like the proxy is refusing to send requests through even though the backend services themselves are healthy and responding fine when we curl them directly. The problem goes away after traffic dies down but comes back every day during peak hours.

We haven't changed any configuration recently. Our backends are running fine -- CPU and memory look normal. It's the proxy layer that seems to be dropping things on the floor.

Can you help us figure out what part of the proxy codebase is responsible for this "overflow" reset and what controls the limits? We need to understand the code path so we can tune the right settings.

Also, please identify any related source files, documentation, or components that are relevant to understanding the full picture (e.g., configuration schemas, related circuit-breaking mechanisms, connection pool internals).

Thanks,
Jordan


Search only these repositories: github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2

Now I have a complete picture. Here is the full analysis.

---

## Root Cause: Circuit Breaker Overflow

The error message `upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. reset reason: overflow` is generated by Envoy's **circuit breaking** system, not a backend failure. The backends are healthy — Envoy is refusing to forward requests because cluster-level resource limits have been hit.

---

## The Code Path (Step by Step)

### 1. Error message is constructed in the router

The exact error string is assembled in [`source/common/router/router.cc`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/source/common/router/router.cc?L1415-L1420), inside `Filter::onUpstreamReset`:

```cpp
const std::string body =
    absl::StrCat("upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. ",
                 (is_retry_ ? "retried and the latest " : ""),
                 "reset reason: ", Http::Utility::resetReasonToString(reset_reason), ...);
```

The `reset_reason` here is `Http::StreamResetReason::Overflow`, which [`resetReasonToString`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/source/common/http/utility.cc?L1029-L1031) maps to the string `"overflow"`.

The router also [explicitly notes](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/source/common/router/router.cc?L1379-L1383) that this reset reason means a cluster-wide resource overflow from circuit breakers — **not** an upstream error — and deliberately skips outlier detection ejection to avoid making the situation worse.

### 2. Overflow is triggered in the connection pool

[`source/common/conn_pool/conn_pool_base.cc`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/source/common/conn_pool/conn_pool_base.cc) has two overflow sites:

**Pending requests overflow** (most likely cause at peak traffic — no ready connection available):
```cpp
// Line 282-287
if (!host_->cluster().resourceManager(priority_).pendingRequests().canCreate()) {
    ENVOY_LOG(debug, "max pending streams overflow");
    onPoolFailure(nullptr, absl::string_view(), ConnectionPool::PoolFailureReason::Overflow, context);
    host_->cluster().trafficStats()->upstream_rq_pending_overflow_.inc();
    return nullptr;
}
```

**Max requests (streams) overflow** (when a connection is available but the cluster's active request limit is hit):
```cpp
// Line 175-180
if (enforceMaxRequests() && !host_->cluster().resourceManager(priority_).requests().canCreate()) {
    ENVOY_LOG(debug, "max streams overflow");
    onPoolFailure(..., ConnectionPool::PoolFailureReason::Overflow, context);
    traffic_stats.upstream_rq_pending_overflow_.inc();
    return;
}
```

Both paths set `PoolFailureReason::Overflow`, which is then translated to `Http::StreamResetReason::Overflow` in [`source/common/router/upstream_request.cc`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/source/common/router/upstream_request.cc?L566-L585).

### 3. The `canCreate()` check

`canCreate()` is defined in [`source/common/common/basic_resource_impl.h`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/source/common/common/basic_resource_impl.h?L29):

```cpp
bool canCreate() override { return current_.load() < max(); }
```

`max()` comes from the cluster's `ResourceManagerImpl` ([`source/common/upstream/resource_manager_impl.h`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/source/common/upstream/resource_manager_impl.h?L74-L94)), which is initialized from the circuit breaker thresholds in the cluster config, with runtime override support via keys like `circuit_breakers.<cluster_name>.<priority>.max_pending_requests`.

### 4. Retries are suppressed

[`source/common/router/retry_state_impl.cc`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/source/common/router/retry_state_impl.cc?L468-L471) explicitly blocks retries for overflow resets:

```cpp
// Never retry if the reset reason is overflow.
if (reset_reason == Http::StreamResetReason::Overflow) {
    return RetryDecision::NoRetry;
}
```

---

## The Relevant Circuit Breaker Thresholds

All thresholds are configured per-cluster, per-priority in [`api/envoy/config/cluster/v3/circuit_breaker.proto`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/api/envoy/config/cluster/v3/circuit_breaker.proto?L57-L99):

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `max_connections` | **1024** | Max upstream TCP connections across all hosts in a cluster |
| `max_pending_requests` | **1024** | Max requests queued waiting for a connection |
| `max_requests` | **1024** | Max parallel in-flight requests (HTTP/2+) |
| `max_retries` | **3** | Max active retries |
| `max_connection_pools` | unlimited | Max concurrent connection pools |

Given the symptom (fails at peak ~2-4pm, recovers when traffic drops), the two most likely culprits are:
- **`max_pending_requests`** — requests pile up waiting for a free connection; when the queue hits 1024, overflow fires
- **`max_connections`** — if the connection limit is also saturated, new connections can't be created to drain the pending queue

---

## Key Statistics to Check

From [`docs/root/configuration/upstream/cluster_manager/cluster_stats.rst`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/docs/root/configuration/upstream/cluster_stats.rst?L60-L83):

- `upstream_rq_pending_overflow` — increments every time a request is dropped due to pending/request circuit breaker overflow (this is the primary signal)
- `upstream_cx_overflow` — increments every time the connection circuit breaker fires
- `upstream_cx_pool_overflow` — connection pool count overflow

Check these via the Envoy admin endpoint (`/stats` or `/clusters`). The admin clusters endpoint also [reports live circuit breaker state](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/source/server/admin/clusters_handler.cc?L32-L38).

---

## How to Tune

**In your cluster config**, under `circuit_breakers.thresholds`, raise the appropriate limits:

```yaml
circuit_breakers:
  thresholds:
    - priority: DEFAULT
      max_connections: 4096         # raise from default 1024
      max_pending_requests: 4096    # raise from default 1024
      max_requests: 4096            # raise from default 1024
```

You can also override at runtime without a restart using the runtime key pattern `circuit_breakers.<cluster_name>.<priority>.max_pending_requests` (documented in [`docs/root/configuration/upstream/cluster_manager/cluster_runtime.rst`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/docs/root/configuration/upstream/cluster_manager/cluster_runtime.rst?L175-L182)).

To effectively disable circuit breaking during testing, see [`docs/root/faq/load_balancing/disable_circuit_breaking.rst`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/docs/root/faq/load_balancing/disable_circuit_breaking.rst) — set thresholds to `1000000000`.

> **Important note from the implementation**: Worker threads share circuit breaker counters, but the implementation is ["eventually consistent"](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/envoy--v1.31.2/-/blob/source/common/upstream/resource_manager_impl.h?L65-L72) — limits may be transiently exceeded due to races across threads. So observed overflow at exactly the limit is expected.
